# B2 Reference Architectures for Commercial Drones: full text

> Generated by tools/generate_catalog.py from the pages listed below; links are relative to the repository root. Product behavior is authoritative at https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage.

<!-- source: docs/commercial-drones.md -->

# Commercial drones on Backblaze B2 (agent-readable)

Catalog updated: 2026-11-16. Current product behavior is authoritative in the [Backblaze B2 documentation](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage). Pricing and egress terms are authoritative on the [B2 pricing page](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing).

## Workload
Commercial drone operators produce imagery, video, telemetry and derived products. They work in survey, construction, mining, agriculture, energy and utility inspection, and insurance. Size each mission from image count, video bitrate and duration, generated products, and retention periods. The lifecycle runs from field offload, through photogrammetry, map and 3D delivery, and AI inspection, to the labeling loop that retrains inspection models.

## Where does B2 fit?
B2 is the S3-compatible system of record across the mission lifecycle:

- **Landing zone:** field offload of raw captures, with manifests and Object Lock for evidence.
- **Processing I/O:** the input source and output sink for stateless photogrammetry and AI workers.
- **Range-read origin:** cloud-native formats (COG, COPC, EPT, Parquet) that GDAL-based tools, PDAL and DuckDB read in place.
- **Training data store:** the labeling loop and versioned training datasets behind inspection models.
- **Archive:** retention-governed storage for client deliverables and evidentiary records.

Delivery is read-heavy downstream. B2 includes egress, and CDN partners such as Cloudflare can front it. See [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for current terms.

## Which architecture do I need?

| Need | Architecture |
|---|---|
| Get SD-card and dock data into one durable place and start processing | [flight-capture-offload](architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md) |
| Run OpenDroneMap or COLMAP against B2 and keep every run | [photogrammetry-processing](architectures/photogrammetry-processing/architecture.md) |
| Serve orthomosaics and DEMs to web maps and GIS without downloads | [cog-map-serving](architectures/cog-map-serving/architecture.md) |
| Stream point clouds, meshes and splats to web viewers | [point-cloud-3d-streaming](architectures/point-cloud-3d-streaming/architecture.md) |
| Detect and geolocate defects in inspection video and query them fleet-wide | [ai-inspection-detection](architectures/ai-inspection-detection/architecture.md) |
| Label frames and publish versioned defect datasets | [inspection-training-data](architectures/inspection-training-data/architecture.md) |

## Can I use B2 with ...?

- **rclone:** yes. Use the native B2 backend, or the S3 backend with a B2 endpoint.
- **OpenDroneMap NodeODM:** set `--s3_endpoint` to the B2 endpoint and `--s3_acl none`. Use a dedicated client staging bucket without a key-prefix restriction for its root probe and task-ID layout; a separate publisher verifies and moves outputs into `products/`.
- **GDAL, rasterio, TiTiler:** yes, through `/vsis3/` with `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT`. Set the variables in the TiTiler container environment.
- **QGIS:** yes. Add a raster layer with protocol type AWS S3 and set `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT` in its credential options, or set the GDAL `AWS_*` variables globally.
- **ArcGIS Pro:** yes. Create a cloud storage connection file with service provider Amazon and the B2 endpoint as the Service End Point.
- **GeoServer:** yes, through the COG community module. Set `IIO_<ALIAS>_AWS_ENDPOINT` to the B2 endpoint.
- **PDAL and Entwine:** yes, through Arbiter with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` set to the host only (`s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`); Arbiter prepends `https://`.
- **DuckDB:** yes. Use the httpfs S3 secret with `ENDPOINT`.
- **CVAT:** yes. Follow CVAT's Backblaze B2 guide: provider Amazon S3 with the B2 Endpoint URL.
- **Label Studio:** yes. Set the S3 Endpoint field on source and target storage.
- **Ultralytics YOLO and Roboflow Inference:** through worker code. They have no storage connector, so the worker moves frames and results with boto3, as in the Backblaze samples.
- **Vendor-cloud workflows:** stage completed mission exports from the provider, then copy them to B2 through a relay using rclone or an SDK.
- **Agisoft Metashape, PIX4Dmatic:** desktop only. Stage data with rclone.

Use the endpoint, authentication, and object-access configuration linked from each integration in the [catalog](catalog/architectures.yaml).

## B2 capabilities that apply
These capabilities apply:

- S3-compatible API with a regional endpoint (`https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region).
- Application keys scoped to one bucket, one name prefix and a set of capabilities.
- Multipart upload, required above 5 GB per object.
- Presigned PUT and GET URLs, with CORS.
- HTTP range GETs.
- Event Notifications: prefix-filtered, optionally signed, enabled through Backblaze Support.
- Lifecycle rules: hide then delete by age, and cancel unfinished large uploads. There are no storage tiers.
- Object Lock (governance or compliance) and legal hold. Object Lock must be enabled on the bucket.
- SSE-B2.
- Included egress.
- CDN origin through Cloudflare.

Cloud Replication is bucket-to-bucket disaster recovery, not client delivery. No architecture here requires it.

## When Overdrive may apply
Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only for sustained, measured high-throughput reads. One example is multi-GPU training on large inspection datasets, or fleet-wide reprocessing, where storage throughput rather than compute is the bottleneck. Field offload is bound by the uplink, photogrammetry by compute, and map and 3D delivery is absorbed by CDNs and tile caches.

## What to keep off B2
These stay off B2:

- SfM scratch, feature databases and keyframe scratch: local NVMe.
- Job queues and event-broker retry state: a queue service.
- Mission and asset registries, work orders and spatial search indexes: Postgres/PostGIS.
- Annotation databases: block storage.
- Tile caches: CDN or Redis.
- Viewer session state: the application.
- Live flight video: RTMP/WebRTC streaming.
- Identity-provider state and application authorization decisions: the identity service and application.

For temporary storage credentials, consult [Backblaze IAM and STS](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-iam-sts-api) and its operation-specific availability. These architectures use scoped application keys or portal-issued presigned URLs for field offload.

## Links
[README](README.md) - [Architecture index](docs/architecture-index.md) - [Related B2 samples](docs/related-b2-samples.md) - [Configuration examples](examples/README.md) - [B2 docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) - [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) - [Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications) - [Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock) - [Lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules) - [Cloudflare integrations](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations) - [Backblaze Labs](https://backblazelabs.com/)

<!-- source: architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md -->

# Offload flight captures into a per-mission archive and trigger processing

## Workload

After each flight, a field laptop, ground station or relay moves captures off SD cards and docks: stills, video, SRT/GPX telemetry, flight logs and RTK/PPK correction files. Capture volume depends on image count, video bitrate and duration, and telemetry frequency. Captures must land once, intact and attributable, in one durable place. Their arrival must start processing reliably, without a file server in the middle.

B2 is the landing zone and system of record for raw captures. Mission ids, pilots, aircraft and work orders live in a database.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SD[SD cards / dock storage] -->|rclone copy, checksums| RAW
  PORTAL[Browser field portal] -->|presigned PUT, stills only| RAW
  VENDOR[DJI FlightHub / vendor cloud] -->|export, then rclone relay| RAW
  RAW[(B2 raw bucket<br/>raw/client/site/mission-id/)]
  RAW -->|Event Notification on raw/ prefix| BROKER[Event broker<br/>filters */manifest.json]
  BROKER -->|enqueue| Q[Job queue - off B2]
  Q --> PHOTO[photogrammetry-processing]
  Q --> AI[ai-inspection-detection]
  REG[(Mission registry<br/>Postgres/PostGIS - off B2)] -.mission id.-> SD
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as Uploader (rclone / portal)
  participant B2 as B2 raw bucket
  participant EB as Event broker
  participant Q as Job queue
  U->>B2: PUT stills, video (multipart), telemetry, logs
  Note over B2: each upload emits an event, which the broker drops
  U->>B2: PUT manifest.json (last)
  B2->>EB: POST event (signed if a secret is set)
  EB->>EB: verify signature, key ends with /manifest.json, dedupe
  EB->>Q: enqueue mission job
  EB-->>B2: 200 quickly
```

1. The field laptop runs `rclone copy` with the native B2 backend from the SD card or a staging folder into `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/`. `<client>` is the customer or business unit that owns the site. rclone verifies checksums and uploads large files in chunks.
2. A browser field portal can upload stills directly with presigned PUT URLs. The [B2 Browser Upload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-browser-upload) sample shows this pattern. A single PUT is capped at 5 GB, so multi-GB video uses multipart upload from rclone or an SDK.
3. The uploader writes `manifest.json` last. It records the mission id, site, aircraft, camera, CRS, and a file list with client-computed hashes.
4. A B2 Event Notification rule on the `raw/` prefix posts to an event broker. Rules filter by prefix only, so the broker drops every event whose key does not end in `/manifest.json` and enqueues one job per mission. Without that filter, each of hundreds of image uploads would trigger a job.
5. DJI Dock and FlightHub fleets land media in the vendor cloud or a self-hosted store first. A relay running rclone then copies it to B2, because DJI's cloud storage options target AWS, Alibaba or a self-hosted store rather than B2 directly.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-raw` | `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/` | Keep all versions; lifecycle cancels unfinished large-file uploads after N days | Enabled on the bucket; governance retention or legal hold for evidentiary missions | Write-once raw captures and `manifest.json` |
| `<org>-drone-raw` | `staging/<crew>/` (optional) | Hide, then delete after N days | None | Partial offloads awaiting a manifest |

Object Lock must be enabled on the bucket before retention can be set on files. Bucket names are globally unique, so prefix them with your organization and expect collisions. B2 has no storage tiers. Lifecycle rules here clean up unfinished uploads and staging objects; they never move captures.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Mission and flight registry, pilot and aircraft records, work orders | Postgres/PostGIS | Transactional, queried by location and time |
| Job queue and broker retry state | A queue service | Needs acknowledgements and retries, not objects |
| SD-card staging during copy | Field laptop disk | Local, temporary |
| Vendor-cloud credentials and export jobs | Relay tier | Use the vendor's export workflow, then upload completed files with scoped B2 application keys |
| Live remote viewing during flight | RTMP/WebRTC streaming | A streaming problem, not object storage |

This design uses application keys for relay uploads. For temporary role credentials, consult [Backblaze IAM and STS](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-iam-sts-api) and confirm the required operations are available for the account.

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API, regional endpoint | Yes | `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region |
| Presigned PUT URLs and CORS | Yes | Portal uploads of stills; CORS limited to the portal origin ([`examples/cors-field-portal.json`](examples/cors-field-portal.json)) |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Required for objects over 5 GB; rclone and SDKs handle it |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | One write-and-list key per crew or relay (`writeFiles,listFiles`; rclone lists to skip existing files), bucket plus `raw/<client>/` prefix |
| Event Notifications | Yes | Prefix-filtered; enabled through Backblaze Support; optional signing secret |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | `daysFromStartingToCancelingUnfinishedLargeFiles`; optional staging expiry ([`examples/lifecycle-raw.json`](examples/lifecycle-raw.json)) |
| Object Lock and legal hold | Yes | Evidentiary missions ([`examples/object-lock-evidence.json`](examples/object-lock-evidence.json)) |
| SSE-B2 | Optional | Default bucket encryption |
| Cloud Replication | Not used | Bucket-to-bucket DR only; add if policy requires a second region |
| CDN, Overdrive | Not used | Upload path is bound by the field uplink |

## Integration configuration

### rclone (native B2 backend)

- Configure a `b2` remote with an application key ID and key, or an `s3` remote with `provider = Other` and `endpoint = https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Derive the region from the bucket; never copy one from an example.
- Use a key restricted to `<org>-drone-raw` and `raw/<client>/` with `listFiles,writeFiles` (add `readFiles` if `--checksum` comparisons need reads). Do not give field keys `deleteFiles`.
- Use `rclone copy`, not `rclone sync`, so a mistaken local deletion never propagates.
- Setup: the [Backblaze rclone guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2) and the [rclone B2 docs](https://rclone.org/b2/).

### boto3 (field portal and SDK uploads)

- `boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=f"https://s3.{B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com")` with keys held server-side. Browsers receive only presigned PUT URLs with a short TTL.
- Use `TransferConfig` managed multipart for video.
- The [OpenDroneMap sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/opendronemap-photogrammetry-pipeline) demonstrates worker uploads through the B2 S3-compatible API.

### Event broker

- The [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) sample validates signed notifications and fans them out. Put the `*/manifest.json` filter there.
- Deliveries can repeat. Make the enqueue idempotent on `(bucket, key, version id)`.
- See [`examples/event-notifications-raw.json`](examples/event-notifications-raw.json).

## Security

- Field crews and relays hold prefix-scoped write-and-list keys without object reads or permanent version deletion. `writeFiles` still permits hiding objects or uploading new versions under existing keys. Strict append-only access needs a trusted upload relay that allocates fresh authorized keys and refuses replacements. Presigned PUTs limit the method and key but can be replayed until expiry. Object Lock protects retained versions but does not prevent hiding or a new current version.
- Bucket, lifecycle and Object Lock changes need an administrative key. Run them once from provisioning and keep that key out of field devices.
- Verify the `X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature` header when a signing secret is configured.
- Treat presigned URLs as bearer credentials.
- Keep secrets in a gitignored `0600` `.env`; never print keys.

## References

- [Backblaze: integrate rclone with B2](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2)
- [rclone B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/)
- [B2 Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- [B2 large files](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-large-files)
- Samples: [OpenDroneMap Photogrammetry Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/opendronemap-photogrammetry-pipeline), [B2 Browser Upload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-browser-upload), [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker)

<!-- source: architectures/photogrammetry-processing/architecture.md -->

# Reconstruct orthomosaics, elevation models, point clouds and meshes from mission imagery

## Workload

Stateless CPU or GPU workers turn a mission's overlapping images into survey products: an orthomosaic, a DSM/DTM, a LAZ point cloud, a textured mesh and a quality report. The engine is structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo, using OpenDroneMap NodeODM or COLMAP. Size worker scratch space and archived products from the selected output formats and reconstruction settings. Teams reprocess when parameters or software change, so every run's outputs must sit next to its inputs without a shared filesystem.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  RAW[(B2 raw<br/>raw/client/site/mission-id/)] -->|S3 GET| W[Worker<br/>local NVMe scratch]
  W -->|pyodm| ODM[NodeODM]
  W -->|pycolmap| COL[COLMAP]
  ODM -->|S3 upload, --s3_acl none| STAGE[(B2 NodeODM staging<br/>dedicated bucket per client)]
  STAGE -->|read completed task outputs| W
  W -->|publish finished products| PROD
  COL -->|boto3 managed multipart| PROD
  DESK[Metashape / PIX4Dmatic desktop] <-->|rclone stage in / push exports| PROD
  PROD[(B2 products<br/>products/mission-id/run-id/)] -->|run manifest.json last| EV[Event broker]
  EV --> COG[cog-map-serving]
  EV --> PC[point-cloud-3d-streaming]
  EV --> AI[ai-inspection-detection]
```

1. An event (see [flight-capture-offload](architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md)) or an operator triggers a job for `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/`.
2. The worker downloads images to local NVMe. SfM scratch, feature databases and temporary tiles never go to B2.
3. NodeODM uploads task results to a dedicated private `<org>-drone-nodeodm-<client>` bucket. Give its key access to that bucket without a name prefix: startup writes `test.txt` at the bucket root and results use task-ID paths. Configure `--s3_endpoint`, `--s3_bucket`, `--s3_upload_everything`, and `--s3_acl none`; pass credentials through the environment.
4. The publisher reads completed NodeODM outputs with a separate staging-reader key, or uses local COLMAP results, and uploads them with a products-writer key to `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/{orthophoto,dsm,dtm,pointcloud,mesh,report}/`.
5. A run `manifest.json`, written last, records software versions, parameters, the input manifest hash and the output keys. A new run id per execution keeps earlier runs immutable.
6. Desktop tools without S3 support, such as Agisoft Metashape and PIX4Dmatic, stay local. rclone stages inputs down and pushes exported products into the same layout.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-raw` | `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/` | Read-only here | As in flight-capture-offload | Inputs |
| `<org>-drone-nodeodm-<client>` | `<task-id>/` and root `test.txt` | Expire staging after the publication window ([lifecycle-nodeodm.json](examples/lifecycle-nodeodm.json)) | None | Native NodeODM task layout and connection probe |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/` | Immutable per run; optional lifecycle to expire superseded runs | Optional for contractual deliverables | Orthomosaic, DSM/DTM, LAZ, mesh, report, run manifest |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `staging/<job-id>/` | Hide after N days, then delete | None | Desktop-tool exports awaiting review |

Lifecycle rules apply by prefix and age. They cannot keep the last K runs. Expire superseded runs from a job that reads the run manifests, or set lifecycle on a `superseded/` prefix that the job copies into.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SfM working directories, feature and match databases, temporary tiles | Local NVMe | Random I/O and in-place edits |
| NodeODM/WebODM task state, job queue | Their own stores | Transactional |
| Pix4Dcloud and DroneDeploy projects | Vendor clouds | No customer-configurable S3 endpoint found; B2 receives exports only |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API, regional endpoint | Yes | NodeODM `--s3_endpoint`, boto3 `endpoint_url` |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB GeoTIFF, LAZ and mesh outputs |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Read the client raw prefix; NodeODM writes its dedicated bucket; the publisher reads staging and writes `products/` |
| Event Notifications | Yes | Run manifest triggers downstream jobs ([`examples/event-notifications-products.json`](examples/event-notifications-products.json)) |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire staging and superseded runs ([`examples/lifecycle-products.json`](examples/lifecycle-products.json)) |
| Object Lock | Optional | Contractual deliverables |
| Presigned URLs, CORS | Not here | Delivery is covered in cog-map-serving and point-cloud-3d-streaming |
| Overdrive | Not used | Reconstruction is compute-bound |

## Integration configuration

### OpenDroneMap NodeODM

```bash
# Run with the nodeodm-writer credential for this client
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$B2_APPLICATION_KEY"
export AWS_REGION="$B2_REGION"
node index.js \
  --s3_endpoint "s3.${B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com" \
  --s3_bucket "$ORG-drone-nodeodm-$CLIENT" \
  --s3_upload_everything --s3_acl none
```

- Source: [`config.js`](https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/NodeODM/blob/master/config.js) documents the flags. [`libs/S3.js`](https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/NodeODM/blob/master/libs/S3.js) passes the endpoint to `AWS.Endpoint`. NodeODM also falls back to `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Prefer those environment variables over command-line flags, which can show up in process listings.
- Use a dedicated bucket per client or trusted NodeODM deployment. A `products/`-restricted key cannot perform the root connection probe. The publisher uploads completed task outputs into `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/`, verifies them, and writes the run manifest last. Complete publication before the staging lifecycle expires the task outputs.
- NodeODM's default ACL is `public-read`; always pass `--s3_acl none`.

### COLMAP / pycolmap

COLMAP has no storage layer. The [COLMAP Photogrammetry Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/colmap-photogrammetry-archive) sample stages inputs and archives the database, sparse model and point cloud with boto3 against the B2 endpoint. The B2 connection is the sample's code, not COLMAP's.

### rclone for desktop tools

Use one key restricted to `staging/` with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` and push exports with `rclone copy`. See [flight-capture-offload](architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md#rclone-native-b2-backend).

## Security

- Never leave NodeODM's default `public-read` ACL in place.
- The processing key reads only `raw/<client>/` and cannot delete captures. Keep NodeODM staging credentials separate from the publisher's staging-reader and products-writer credentials.
- Run manifests carry input hashes, so every product traces back to its captures.
- Keep keys in environment variables or a `0600` `.env`, never on the command line or in logs.

## References

- [NodeODM](https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/NodeODM)
- [COLMAP](https://colmap.github.io/)
- [B2 large files and multipart](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-large-files)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- Samples: [OpenDroneMap Photogrammetry Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/opendronemap-photogrammetry-pipeline), [COLMAP Photogrammetry Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/colmap-photogrammetry-archive), [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker)

<!-- source: architectures/cog-map-serving/architecture.md -->

# Serve orthomosaics and elevation models as cloud-optimized map layers

## Workload

Clients and analysts view and analyze multi-GB orthomosaics, DEMs and multispectral index maps such as NDVI without downloading them. Each product is stored once as a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) with internal overviews. Tile servers, desktop GIS and Python read only the byte ranges they need. No XYZ tile pyramid is pre-rendered or stored.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  PROD[(B2 products<br/>products/mission-id/run-id/)] -->|/vsis3/ read| CONV[COG conversion<br/>rio-cogeo / gdal_translate -of COG]
  CONV -->|/vsis3/ write| COG[(B2 cog/mission-id/product.tif)]
  COG -->|range GET| TT[TiTiler<br/>validated layer ids]
  COG -->|range GET| GIS[QGIS / ArcGIS Pro / GeoServer]
  COG -->|range GET| AN[Analytics jobs<br/>segmentation, change detection]
  AN --> ANA[(B2 analysis/mission-id/)]
  TT --> CACHE[CDN / tile cache - off B2]
  COG -->|origin| CF[Cloudflare CDN or signing Worker]
  CF --> WEB[Public or client map viewers]
  COG -->|short-lived presigned GET| CLIENT[Client download]
```

1. A conversion job reads `products/<mission-id>/<run-id>/orthophoto.tif`. It writes a COG to `cog/<mission-id>/<product>.tif` through GDAL `/vsis3/`, with `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT` pointed at B2, using `rio cogeo create` or `gdal_translate -of COG`.
2. TiTiler renders XYZ/WMTS tiles on demand from range GETs. It accepts only validated layer ids that map to keys, never raw URLs.
3. Desktop and server GIS open the same objects in place: QGIS through `/vsis3/`, ArcGIS Pro through a cloud storage connection file, and GeoServer through the COG community module.
4. Optional analytics jobs read windows and write masks and GeoJSON to `analysis/<mission-id>/`. Examples are SAM-based segmentation and change detection between repeat survey flights.
5. Public basemaps go through Cloudflare with B2 as origin. Private deliverables go out as short-lived presigned GETs, or through a Worker that signs requests to a private bucket.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-products` | `cog/<mission-id>/` | Overwrite only by publishing a new mission or run; expire superseded layers by job | Optional for contracted deliverables | One COG per product |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `analysis/<mission-id>/` | Kept with the mission; no age expiry | None | Masks, GeoJSON, change maps (deliverables) |
| `<org>-drone-public` (optional) | `basemaps/<layer-id>/` | Keep current only | None | Cleared imagery served publicly through the CDN |

Keep public and private data in separate buckets. Bucket visibility is set per bucket, not per prefix.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rendered tile cache | CDN or Redis | Hot, short-lived, regenerable |
| Layer registry, render configs, styles | Database or config store | Small, transactional |
| Map server configuration and user auth | Map server, identity provider | Not object data |
| Pre-rendered XYZ pyramids | Not stored | Rendered on demand from COGs |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3 API with HTTP range GETs | Yes | GDAL `/vsis3/` reads COG headers and tiles by range |
| Presigned GET URLs | Yes | Time-limited client delivery |
| CORS rules | Yes | Browser map clients reading presigned COG URLs |
| Scoped read-only keys | Yes | One per tile server, GIS group or Worker, restricted to `cog/` |
| CDN origin (Cloudflare) | Yes | See [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for egress terms through partner CDNs |
| Included egress | Yes | Downstream delivery is read-heavy; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Multipart upload | Yes | GDAL and rio-cogeo writes of large COGs |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Trigger conversion when a run manifest lands |
| Object Lock, Cloud Replication | Not used | Products are covered upstream |
| Overdrive | Consider only if measured | Tile caches normally absorb repeated reads |

## Integration configuration

All endpoints are derived from the bucket region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Never hardcode one.

### GDAL `/vsis3/`

```bash
export AWS_S3_ENDPOINT="s3.${B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com"   # host only, no scheme
export AWS_REGION="$B2_REGION"
export AWS_VIRTUAL_HOSTING=TRUE                            # B2 supports virtual-hosted-style requests
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="<application-key-id>" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="<application-key>"
gdal_translate -of COG /vsis3/$BUCKET/products/$MISSION/$RUN/orthophoto.tif /vsis3/$BUCKET/cog/$MISSION/ortho.tif
```

Writing COGs directly to `/vsis3/` depends on the GDAL version and driver. Writing locally and uploading is the conservative path. See the [GDAL virtual file systems](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/virtual_file_systems.html) documentation.

### Rasterio and rio-cogeo

Pass `rasterio.session.AWSSession(endpoint_url="s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com")` to `rasterio.Env`; it sets GDAL's `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT` ([source](https://github.com/rasterio/rasterio/blob/main/rasterio/session.py)). The environment variables above also work, and `rio cogeo create` writes COGs straight to `/vsis3/` paths.

### TiTiler

TiTiler reads COGs through GDAL, so set the `AWS_*` configuration above in the TiTiler container environment. The [TiTiler COG Map Tiles](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/titiler-cog-map-tiles) sample derives the endpoint from `B2_REGION`. Give TiTiler a read-only key scoped to `cog/`, and map layer ids to keys server-side.

### QGIS

Add a raster layer with protocol type **AWS S3**, bucket `<bucket>` and object key `cog/<mission-id>/ortho.tif`, and set `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT=s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` in the layer's credential options ([QGIS docs](https://docs.qgis.org/latest/en/docs/user_manual/managing_data_source/opening_data.html)). To share one configuration across layers, set the GDAL `AWS_*` variables globally under Settings → Options → Variables or in the environment. Give each GIS user group a read-only key scoped to `cog/`.

### Esri ArcGIS Pro

Run **Create Cloud Storage Connection File** with service provider Amazon, the bucket name, a read-only key scoped to `cog/`, and **Service End Point** `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Esri documents the custom endpoint for S3-compatible object storage ([Esri docs](https://doc.esri.com/en/arcgis-pro/latest/tool-reference/data-management/create-cloud-storage-connection-file.html)). Reference rasters through the resulting `.acs` file.

### GeoServer COG community module

Set `IIO_<SCHEME>_AWS_ENDPOINT` with `_AWS_USER`, `_AWS_PASSWORD` and `_AWS_REGION`, where `<SCHEME>` is the scheme of the layer URL. GeoServer keeps one S3 client per region and scheme alias.

```bash
# Layers addressed as s3://<bucket>/cog/<mission-id>/ortho.tif
IIO_S3_AWS_ENDPOINT="https://s3.${B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com"
IIO_S3_AWS_REGION="$B2_REGION"
IIO_S3_AWS_USER="<application-key-id>" IIO_S3_AWS_PASSWORD="<application-key>"

# Layers addressed as https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<bucket>/cog/... use the HTTPS alias
IIO_HTTPS_AWS_ENDPOINT="https://s3.${B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com"
IIO_HTTPS_AWS_REGION="$B2_REGION"
IIO_HTTPS_AWS_USER="<application-key-id>" IIO_HTTPS_AWS_PASSWORD="<application-key>"
```

GeoServer documents `IIO_<ALIAS>_AWS_ENDPOINT` for third-party S3-compatible services; set it to the full `https://` endpoint as above. Install the COG community module, which ships separately from GeoServer releases ([GeoServer docs](https://docs-archive.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/community/cog/cog.html)).

### Cloudflare CDN and Workers

- **Public bucket:** proxy a custom domain to the bucket's friendly URL. See the [Backblaze Cloudflare guides](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations).
- **Private bucket:** the [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2) Worker signs S3 requests with a read-only key scoped to `cog/` and passes `Range` headers through.

## Security

- Tile servers accept layer ids, never arbitrary URLs. Otherwise `/vsis3/` and `/vsicurl/` become a server-side request forgery path.
- Each consumer gets its own read-only key scoped to `cog/` or narrower. Analytics writers are scoped to `analysis/`.
- Treat presigned URLs as bearer credentials. Restrict CORS to exact map-viewer origins, with `GET` and `HEAD` only (see [`examples/cors-map-viewers.json`](examples/cors-map-viewers.json)).
- Publish only cleared imagery to the public bucket.

## References

- [GDAL virtual file systems](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/virtual_file_systems.html)
- [rio-cogeo](https://github.com/cogeotiff/rio-cogeo)
- [TiTiler](https://github.com/developmentseed/titiler)
- [Backblaze Cloudflare integrations](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations)
- [B2 CORS rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cross-origin-resource-sharing-rules)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)
- Samples: [TiTiler COG Map Tiles](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/titiler-cog-map-tiles), [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2)

<!-- source: architectures/point-cloud-3d-streaming/architecture.md -->

# Convert point clouds and meshes into streamable 3D datasets for web viewers

## Workload

Photogrammetric and drone-LiDAR point clouds run from hundreds of MB to hundreds of GB per site or corridor. Construction, mining and utility clients use them for digital twins, volume measurement and progress tracking, but cannot work with them as downloads. Teams convert them to range-readable formats next to the source data:

- COPC (Cloud Optimized Point Cloud) for single-file streaming.
- EPT (Entwine Point Tile) for very large or multi-flight sites.

Meshes and Gaussian splats are versioned alongside.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SRC[(B2 pointcloud/mission-id/run-id/raw/<br/>LAS/LAZ from NodeODM or LiDAR)] -->|s3:// via Arbiter| PDAL[PDAL pipeline<br/>filter, classify, reproject]
  PDAL -->|writers.copc to s3://| COPC[(B2 pointcloud/mission-id/run-id/copc/)]
  SRC -->|s3:// via Arbiter| ENT[Entwine build]
  ENT --> EPT[(B2 pointcloud/site/ept/)]
  TWIN[Twin jobs<br/>COLMAP, gsplat, mesh] --> TW[(B2 twins/site/capture-id/)]
  COPC -->|range GET| CDN[Public bucket + CORS<br/>or CDN / signing Worker]
  EPT --> CDN
  TW --> CDN
  CDN --> VIEW[Potree / CesiumJS / COPC viewers]
  BIM[(IFC/BIM models)] -.progress comparison.-> TW
```

1. Source LAS/LAZ from NodeODM ([photogrammetry-processing](architectures/photogrammetry-processing/architecture.md)) or a LiDAR payload lands in `pointcloud/<mission-id>/<run-id>/raw/`.
2. A PDAL pipeline filters, classifies and reprojects the cloud. It reads `s3://` input and writes `.copc.laz` back through Arbiter, with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (host only; Arbiter prepends `https://`).
3. For multi-flight or very large sites, Entwine builds an EPT index into `pointcloud/<site>/ept/` through the same Arbiter S3 driver.
4. Digital-twin jobs version camera poses, `transforms.json`, meshes and `.ply` splats under `twins/<site>/<capture-id>/`. The COLMAP Gaussian Splatting sample shows this pattern.
5. Viewers such as Potree, CesiumJS and COPC viewers fetch by HTTP URL. They read from a public bucket with CORS, or through a CDN or signing Worker. Per-file presigned URLs are impractical for multi-file octrees.
6. Optionally, the twin is compared against IFC/BIM models to track construction progress. The IfcOpenShell BIM Archive sample shows this pattern.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-products` | `pointcloud/<mission-id>/<run-id>/raw/` | Immutable per run | Optional | Source LAS/LAZ |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `pointcloud/<mission-id>/<run-id>/copc/` | Immutable per run; expire superseded runs by job | None | COPC for streaming |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `pointcloud/<site>/ept/` | Rebuilt per site version; lifecycle expires old builds under a dated prefix | None | EPT for very large sites |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `twins/<site>/<capture-id>/` | Immutable per capture | None | Poses, meshes, splats, run manifest |
| `<org>-drone-public` (optional) | `tilesets/<dataset-id>/` | Keep current only | None | Cleared datasets served publicly |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PostGIS footprints and spatial search indexes | Database | Queried by geometry |
| Viewer session state | Application | Per-user and transient |
| Cesium ion-hosted assets | Cesium ion | Import and export are AWS-only; no B2 endpoint |
| PDAL and Entwine processing scratch | Local disk | Temporary |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3 API with HTTP range GETs | Yes | COPC and EPT are read by range and by file |
| CORS rules | Yes | Viewer origins, `GET` and `HEAD` |
| Public bucket or CDN origin | Yes | Multi-file tilesets need stable URLs |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB COPC and LAZ |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Processing writes `pointcloud/` and `twins/`; Worker reads only |
| Presigned URLs | Limited | Single-file COPC only; impractical for EPT octrees |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Trigger conversion when a run manifest lands |
| Object Lock, Cloud Replication, Overdrive | Not used | Not required for derived 3D products |

## Integration configuration

### PDAL (via Arbiter)

```bash
export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL="s3.${B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com"   # host only: Arbiter prepends https://
export AWS_REGION="$B2_REGION"                             # Arbiter otherwise defaults to us-east-1
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="<application-key-id>" AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="<application-key>"
pdal translate s3://$BUCKET/pointcloud/$MISSION/$RUN/raw/cloud.laz \
               s3://$BUCKET/pointcloud/$MISSION/$RUN/copc/cloud.copc.laz --writers.copc.forward=all
```

Arbiter's `S3::Config::extractBaseUrl` uses `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` verbatim as the base URL, or an `endpoint` key from its JSON config. `S3::Resource::url()` then builds `"https://" + base` and `host()` sends the base as the Host header, so the value must be the host without a scheme; `https://s3...` yields `https://https://s3...` and fails signing. Arbiter uses virtual-hosted style unless the bucket name has dots or `AWS_VIRTUAL_HOSTING=FALSE`; B2 accepts either style. See the [vendored source](https://github.com/PDAL/PDAL/blob/master/vendor/arbiter/arbiter.cpp) and [upstream `s3.cpp`](https://github.com/connormanning/arbiter/blob/master/arbiter/drivers/s3.cpp). For writers that only accept local paths in your PDAL build, write to local scratch and upload with rclone or boto3.

### Entwine

Entwine reads and writes `s3://` paths through the same Arbiter driver ([source](https://github.com/connormanning/arbiter/blob/master/arbiter/drivers/s3.cpp)), so configure the same environment variables above.

### Viewers and delivery

Potree, CesiumJS and COPC viewers consume HTTP URLs and have no S3 connector. Choose one delivery path:

- A public bucket with CORS, for cleared datasets.
- A Cloudflare CDN in front of the public bucket.
- The [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2) Worker signing requests to a private bucket.

## Security

- Keep source clouds and twins private. Publish only cleared datasets to `<org>-drone-public`.
- Processing uses one key per prefix (`pointcloud/` and `twins/`), since a B2 key carries a single name prefix. The Worker key is read-only.
- CORS lists exact viewer origins (see [`examples/cors-map-viewers.json`](examples/cors-map-viewers.json)).
- Site scans can expose security-sensitive infrastructure. Classify them before publishing.

## References

- [PDAL](https://pdal.io)
- [Entwine](https://github.com/connormanning/entwine)
- [COPC specification](https://copc.io)
- [Potree](https://github.com/potree/potree)
- [Backblaze Cloudflare integrations](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloudflare-integrations)
- [B2 CORS rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cross-origin-resource-sharing-rules)
- Samples: [Open3D Point Cloud Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/open3d-point-cloud-pipeline), [COLMAP Gaussian Splatting Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/colmap-gaussian-splatting-pipeline), [IfcOpenShell BIM Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/ifcopenshell-bim-archive), [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2)

<!-- source: architectures/ai-inspection-detection/architecture.md -->

# Detect and geolocate defects in inspection imagery and video

## Workload

Inspection drones fly towers, power lines, solar farms, wind blades, bridges and roofs. Detection models scan the video and stills, and each detection is geotagged from the flight's GPS track. One inspection video fans out into hundreds of derived objects, across thousands of assets per season. Operators need results tied to source media and location, queryable across the fleet, and reprocessable in batch when a better model ships.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  RAW[(B2 raw<br/>video + SRT/GPX + manifest.json)] -->|manifest event| Q[Job queue - off B2]
  Q --> W[GPU worker<br/>Ultralytics YOLO]
  RAW -->|S3 GET stream| W
  W -->|boto3 PUT / multipart| INS[(B2 inspections/asset-id/inspection-id/<br/>keyframes, JSON, GeoJSON)]
  EDGE[Ground station / dock<br/>Roboflow Inference] -->|flagged frames + predictions| SUM[(B2 summaries/device/ Parquet<br/>edge/device/ frames)]
  INS --> PQ[(B2 detections/ Parquet roll-ups)]
  PQ -->|httpfs range reads| DUCK[DuckDB]
  SUM --> DUCK
  DUCK -->|COPY TO s3://| SLICE[(B2 query-slices/)]
  INS -->|presigned GET| UI[Review UI]
  REG[(Asset registry, work orders - off B2)] -.-> UI
  NEW[New model version] -->|batch reprocess| INS2[(B2 inspections/.../model-version/)]
```

1. Source video and SRT/GPX telemetry land in `raw/` (see [flight-capture-offload](architectures/flight-capture-offload/architecture.md)). The manifest event enqueues an inference job.
2. The worker streams the video from B2, samples keyframes, runs Ultralytics YOLO on a local GPU, and extracts the GPS track from sidecar telemetry.
3. It writes annotated keyframes, per-frame detection JSON, `summary.json` and a GeoJSON track to `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/`. The review UI reads them by presigned GET.
4. Edge variant (B2-side pattern): Roboflow Inference runs on the ground station or dock computer. It archives only flagged frames and prediction JSON, with hourly Parquet roll-ups under `summaries/<device>/`. The Roboflow sample is built around cameras; the same pattern fits a dock computer.
5. A roll-up job appends detection rows to Parquet under `detections/`. DuckDB httpfs, with an S3 secret whose `ENDPOINT` is the B2 endpoint, queries the Parquet fleet-wide and writes slices back to `query-slices/` with `COPY ... TO 's3://...'`.
6. When a better model ships, a batch job (see the YOLO11 Batch Detection Pipeline sample) reprocesses the archive under a new model-version prefix. Earlier results are never overwritten.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-raw` | `raw/<client>/<site>/<mission-id>/` | As in flight-capture-offload | As in flight-capture-offload | Source video and telemetry |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `inspections/<asset-id>/<inspection-id>/<model-version>/` | Immutable per model version | Governance or legal hold for evidentiary inspections | Keyframes, JSON, GeoJSON, summary |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `edge/<device>/`, `summaries/<device>/` | Hide unflagged or aged edge frames after N days, then delete | None | Edge-archived frames and Parquet roll-ups |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `detections/` | Append new partitions; compaction job replaces old files | None | Fleet-wide Parquet |
| `<org>-drone-products` | `query-slices/` | Expire after N days | None | DuckDB result slices (throwaway) |

Lifecycle cannot delete files under active Object Lock retention or legal hold.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Asset registry, work orders, defect review status | Database | Transactional, edited by people |
| Inference job queue | Queue service | Acknowledgements and retries |
| Model weights at inference time | Local GPU disk cache | Loaded per job; canonical weights live in `models/` (see [inspection-training-data](architectures/inspection-training-data/architecture.md)) |
| Frame decoding and keyframe scratch | Local disk | Temporary |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3 API, regional endpoint | Yes | boto3 `endpoint_url` derived from `B2_REGION` |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB inspection video |
| Presigned GET | Yes | Review UI media |
| Event Notifications | Yes | Manifest event enqueues inference |
| HTTP range reads | Yes | DuckDB reads Parquet footers and row groups |
| Object Lock / legal hold | Yes | Evidentiary inspection records |
| Scoped keys | Yes | Write-only per edge device; read-only for analysts |
| CORS | Optional | Only if the review UI reads presigned URLs from the browser |
| CDN, Cloud Replication, Overdrive | Not used | Review traffic is internal and modest |

## Integration configuration

### boto3 in Ultralytics and Roboflow pipelines

- Set `endpoint_url=f"https://s3.{B2_REGION}.backblazeb2.com"`, with an optional `B2_ENDPOINT` override. This matches the [YOLO Drone Footage Detection](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo-drone-footage-detection) sample.
- Stream video with managed multipart, and serve review media by presigned GET with a short TTL.
- Workers use a key restricted to `inspections/` with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles`. They read `raw/` with a separate read-only key, because one key covers one prefix.
- Each edge device gets a write-only key restricted to `edge/<device>/` (and a second for `summaries/<device>/`), or presigned PUTs from a site service.

### DuckDB httpfs

```sql
-- Values are templated from configuration; never commit them. <region> comes from the bucket.
CREATE SECRET b2 (
  TYPE s3,
  KEY_ID '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID>',
  SECRET '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY>',
  REGION '<region>',
  ENDPOINT 's3.<region>.backblazeb2.com'
);
SELECT asset_id, class, count(*) FROM read_parquet('s3://<bucket>/detections/**/*.parquet') GROUP BY ALL;
```

DuckDB documents `ENDPOINT` for custom S3 endpoints ([httpfs S3 API](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html)). The [DuckDB Query In Place](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/duckdb-query-in-place) sample corroborates it against B2. Keep the secret in memory (the default `CREATE SECRET`) rather than `CREATE PERSISTENT SECRET`, which writes it to disk.

## Security

- Edge devices hold only write-only, prefix-scoped keys, or presigned PUTs.
- Analysts get read-only keys on `detections/` and `summaries/`. Only the slice writer can write `query-slices/`. A B2 key carries one prefix, so analysts hold one read key per prefix.
- Reprocessing writes a new model-version prefix and never overwrites earlier results.
- Use governance-mode Object Lock or legal hold for inspections that support regulatory or insurance claims. Choose compliance mode only when a contract or regulation requires it.

## References

- [Ultralytics](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics)
- [Roboflow Inference](https://github.com/roboflow/inference)
- [DuckDB httpfs S3 API](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications)
- Samples: [YOLO Drone Footage Detection](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo-drone-footage-detection), [Roboflow Inference Frame Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/roboflow-inference-frame-archive), [YOLO11 Batch Detection Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo11-batch-detection-pipeline), [DuckDB Query In Place](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/duckdb-query-in-place), [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker)

<!-- source: architectures/inspection-training-data/architecture.md -->

# Label inspection frames and publish versioned defect-detection datasets

## Workload

Defect classes are rare and site-specific: cracks, corrosion, vegetation encroachment, thermal hot spots, broken insulators. Inspection teams relabel and retrain continuously. They need labeling tools that read media from the archive without copying it, and dataset versions that are reproducible and tied to the model versions trained on them.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  INS[(B2 inspections/ frames<br/>cog/ orthomosaic chips)] --> CUR[Curation job<br/>select, chip, fastdup]
  CUR -->|duplicates/outliers| QUAR[(B2 curation/quarantine/)]
  CUR --> CAND[(B2 curation/candidates/batch/)]
  CAND --> SAM[SAM 2 pre-labeling]
  SAM --> DRAFT[(B2 labels/draft/batch/)]
  CAND -->|Amazon S3 + Endpoint URL| CVAT[CVAT]
  CAND -->|S3 source storage + S3 Endpoint| LS[Label Studio]
  CVAT -->|export| LBL[(B2 labels/reviewed/batch/)]
  LS -->|S3 target storage| LBL
  LBL --> PUB[Publisher<br/>COCO/YOLO + manifest last]
  PUB --> DS[(B2 datasets/name/version/)]
  DS -->|cache shards to local NVMe| TRAIN[Training]
  TRAIN --> MOD[(B2 models/name/version/)]
  MOD --> RE[ai-inspection-detection batch reprocessing]
```

1. A curation job selects candidate frames from `inspections/` and chips orthomosaic tiles from `cog/`. fastdup flags duplicates, outliers and corrupt files and moves them to `curation/quarantine/`; nothing is deleted. The fastdup Dataset Cleaning sample shows this pattern.
2. SAM 2 writes pre-labeled masks into `labels/draft/<batch>/`. The SAM 2 Mask Dataset Builder sample shows this pattern.
3. Labeling runs in one of two tools:
   - **CVAT** attaches the bucket as cloud storage with provider Amazon S3 and the B2 endpoint in the Endpoint URL field. It reads task data from B2 and exports to B2.
   - **Label Studio** syncs source storage from `curation/candidates/` and writes annotations to target storage in `labels/reviewed/`. Both are configured through its S3 Endpoint field. Media reaches browsers either by presigned URL, which needs bucket CORS, or proxied through Label Studio, which does not.
4. A publisher exports reviewed labels as COCO or YOLO to `datasets/<name>/<version>/`. It writes a `manifest.json` last, listing the source object keys and hashes. Versions are never overwritten.
5. Training workers cache shards on local NVMe, write checkpoints to `models/<name>/<version>/`, and record which dataset version they used.
6. New model versions feed batch reprocessing in [ai-inspection-detection](architectures/ai-inspection-detection/architecture.md).

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-drone-ml` | `curation/candidates/<batch>/` | Expire after labeling closes | None | Frames and chips to label |
| `<org>-drone-ml` | `curation/quarantine/` | Keep for review; expire after N days | None | Duplicates, outliers, corrupt files |
| `<org>-drone-ml` | `labels/draft/`, `labels/reviewed/` | Keep versions while labeling is active | None | Pre-labels and tool exports |
| `<org>-drone-ml` | `datasets/<name>/<version>/` | Immutable; manifest written last | Optional governance retention on release | Training-ready dataset versions |
| `<org>-drone-ml` | `models/<name>/<version>/` | Immutable per version | Optional | Checkpoints and model cards |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CVAT and Label Studio databases, queues and caches | Block storage | Transactional application state |
| Experiment-tracking metadata | Tracking server | Queried by run |
| Embedding or vector indexes | Vector database | Low-latency similarity search |
| Training shard cache | Local NVMe | Repeated multi-epoch reads |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| S3 API, regional endpoint | Yes | CVAT Endpoint URL, Label Studio S3 Endpoint |
| Presigned GET | Yes | Label Studio browser media; CVAT reads server-side |
| CORS rules | Yes | Exact labeling-tool origin when browsers read presigned URLs |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Separate source-read, label-write and publisher keys |
| Immutable versioned prefixes with manifests | Yes | B2-side pattern |
| Object Lock | Optional | On released dataset versions |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire candidates and quarantine ([`examples/lifecycle-ml.json`](examples/lifecycle-ml.json)) |
| Overdrive | Consider only if measured | Sustained multi-GPU reads where storage is the bottleneck |
| Event Notifications, CDN, Cloud Replication | Not used | Labeling is human-paced; delivery is internal |

## Integration configuration

### CVAT

Attach cloud storage with **Provider: Amazon S3**, the bucket name, and **Endpoint URL** `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Set the region to the bucket's region. Use a key restricted to `curation/candidates/` with `listFiles,readFiles`. Exports go to `labels/reviewed/` through a separate cloud storage entry with a write-capable key. Follow CVAT's [Backblaze B2 guide](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/#attach-backblaze-b2-storage).

### Label Studio

- **Source storage:** S3 Endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, prefix `curation/candidates/<batch>/`, key with `listFiles,readFiles`.
- **Target storage:** prefix `labels/reviewed/<batch>/`, key with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles`. Do not grant `deleteFiles`.
- With presigned URLs on, add a CORS rule for the Label Studio origin with `GET` and `HEAD` (see [`examples/cors-labeling.json`](examples/cors-labeling.json)). With them off, Label Studio proxies media and no CORS rule is needed.
- Setup: [Label Studio S3 storage](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3); set the S3 Endpoint field on both source and target storage.

## Security

- One key per role: candidate reader, label writer, publisher, trainer reader. Each is restricted to one bucket and prefix.
- Labeling tools never get `deleteFiles`. Quarantine replaces deletion.
- Treat presigned media URLs as bearer credentials, and restrict CORS to the exact tool origin.
- Restrict who can configure storage endpoints in the labeling tools, because a custom endpoint causes the server to make outbound requests.
